description: DONE (folded 2026-07-03 as ef4043a97, audited PASS). settle_demand_cone's ascent-member sort keyed on key.activation.arrow (raw Ty(u32), a process-dependent interner id) — replaced with world.types().display(&arrow), a structural (rendered-type) key that is per-process AND run-to-run deterministic. VERDICT from investigation+audit: SPEED-ONLY, provably order-IRRELEVANT — settle_demand_cone is a true Jacobi fixpoint (each round reads a FROZEN previous-round snapshot; contributions combine via the ShapeDemand/CallableDemand semilattice join, verified idempotent/commutative/associative; dirty-set is value-change-driven, never processing-order-driven), so members order cannot affect the settled answer OR round count. The audit found the sort is even MORE cosmetic than claimed: the sorted members Vec is not consumed by the return value at all (callers iterate the HashMaps directly) — its only effects are internal round-processing sequence and a never-hit round-budget panic diagnostic. Empirically: activation dumps byte-identical across 5+ runs both at base and post-fix on fz_f98_range_map_converges/quicksort/reverse; matrix set unchanged; 1159/0/24. Two follow-up nits ticketed (see below). Fixes the raw-interner-id nondeterminism; the display-key has a narrow latent tie (closure-typed members sharing fn_id) that is harmless to correctness and unobserved.
title: settle_demand_cone sorts ascent members by raw interned Ty (process-hash-dependent convergence order)
